codeReview.summary: I reviewed the feature metadata, worker handoff/transcript skeleton, the current GPUISceneBridge implementation, and the latest bridge-related committed diff touching these files (`ddddac2`) because the handoff still reports `commitId: pending`. The clip-stack, replace/pop, and unsupported-draw-command handling look coherent, but VAL-SCENE-011 is not fully satisfied: the bridge's documented fallback behavior disagrees with the actual code/tests, and the focused test surface does not cover the unsupported blend-mode fallback that the contract explicitly calls out.

issues.description: The bridge's own soft-failure documentation is out of sync with the implemented fallback behavior. Lines 42-43 say non-rect clips (including path clips) fall back to a bounding rect and radial/conic gradients fall back to the gradient start color, but the implementation below uses a full-surface no-op for `.path` clips (lines 108-110) and leaves radial/conic fills on `cmd.color` instead of the gradient start color (lines 186-211). Since VAL-SCENE-011 requires explicit documented fallback behavior, this feature currently documents the wrong behavior for two unsupported-style cases.

The VAL-SCENE-011 focused tests cover gradients and non-rect clips, but they never exercise a non-default `blendMode` even though the validation contract explicitly includes unsupported blend semantics and the bridge comment documents blend modes as an intentional fallback (`GPUISceneBridge.swift:44`). That leaves one required soft-failure path unproven, so a regression in ignored blend handling would currently ship undetected.
